q: How much coal does a Lucknow brick kiln burn per lakh bricks, and what is the cluster's CO2?
title: Lucknow brick kilns: coal per lakh bricks
short: About 16 to 17 t. TERI's Lucknow profile puts a typical Bull's trench kiln at 27,000 bricks a day for 180 days: 48.6 lakh bricks on 826 t of coal, roughly 1,450 t CO2 a season. The cluster's 230 or so kilns burn about 186,676 t of coal a year.
audience: Brick kiln owners around Lucknow and the Lucknow Brick Kiln Association

ul: About 230 kilns, almost all fixed chimney Bull's trench kilns; about 10 already fire zigzag.
Firing runs about six months, January to June, at 1,000 to 1,100 C; chimney gas leaves at 80 to 120 C.
Hand moulded solid bricks of 9 x 4 x 3 inch, about 3.0 kg each, sun dried before firing.
Class 1 is about 45% of output; Tamda 20%, Class 2, Class 3 and Tukda 10% each, Kali Peti 5%. Every broken or underfired brick burnt the same coal.
Coal is almost the whole energy bill. Diesel only runs the pump set for moulding water.

sections.h: Measure MJ per kg, not only tonnes per lakh
p: Tonnes per lakh moves with brick weight and coal quality. TERI measured Lucknow kilns at 1.38 MJ per kg of fired brick, against 1.1 to 1.2 MJ for a well run kiln. Closing that gap is about one sixth of your coal.

ul: Feeding: crush coal to about 10 mm, feed small amounts every 20 minutes instead of every 45 to 60, use 750 to 1,000 g spoons, one fireman feeding, three or more lines at a time.
Sealing: close wickets with two-brick walls plastered both sides, close side flues, keep about 7 inches of ash on top of the setting.
Zigzag firing: a longer fire path and turbulent air through the stacking, about 10% less coal.
Each of these is worth about 18,678 t of coal a year across the cluster.

sections.h: What to keep for a lender or buyer
ol: Coal invoices and weighbridge slips for the season.
Bricks fired and sold, by class.
Green bricks lost to rain: TERI reports about 20% in an open yard.
Any wood or sawdust, on its own line as biogenic.

example.title: One Lucknow kiln, one season (estimate)
lines: Coal: 826 t x 1.76 t CO2 = 1,454 t CO2
Per lakh bricks: 1,454 / 48.6 = 29.9 t, or about 300 kg per 1,000 bricks
Better feeding at 10%: 82.6 t coal = 145 t CO2 saved
From 1.38 down to 1.15 MJ per kg: about 138 t coal, 242 t CO2 saved
Cluster: 186,676 t x 1.76 = about 328,550 t CO2
example.note: Coal and output from TERI's Lucknow profile. TERI's own table shows 196,620 t CO2 for the cluster, which implies a lower factor than India's BUR-2 coal factor of 1.76 used here. If you have a lab test of your coal, use it.

senseible: Senseible reads coal invoices and weighbridge slips into season totals with CO2 at India's coal factor, so your tonnes per lakh comes from your own bills, not the cluster average.
